title: Patterns in forage fish mercury concentrations across Northeast US estuaries
summary: Normal-means clustering of fish and environmental measurements across Northeast US estuaries found species- and site-specific patterns in mercury concentrations. Dissolved methylmercury was associated with tissue concentrations in both species, while sediment mercury was influential at contaminated sites. These observational associations do not establish causal drivers.
ai_technology: Normal-means clustering groups fish and environmental mercury patterns across estuaries; it supports regional analysis of site/species covariation.
organization: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency; University of Rhode Island

source_review.scope: Primary source full text, including Methods and Results; first result-bearing version checked against primary publication metadata.

evidence.tested: Field measurements from 38 sites in eight estuarine systems sampled over five years were analyzed with normal-means clustering and site-level environmental covariates.
evidence.unknown: Observational site-level associations; the analysis cannot establish causal sources or generalize beyond sampled estuaries.
evidence.ai_role: Normal-means clustering groups fish and environmental mercury patterns across estuaries; it supports regional analysis of site/species covariation.
